items.title: Sheila Jordan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Well, he‟s not Bud Powell, you know. Uh, „cause I love Bud Powell.

ctx.x: „Cause Skeeter and Mitch were big Monk fans, besides Bird, of course. But I, I don‟t know. I thought the music was so simple. I said, “Well,” you know, even his playing. I said, “Well, you know, he‟s not Bud Powell or…” You know, I was into that whole thing. Well, he‟s not Bud Powell, you know. Uh, „cause I love Bud Powell. But it was… once I started trying to learn his music, I said, “This is the most difficult music that I‟ve ever, ever tried to sing.” His music. And did I get an eye-opener. Did I get a lesson,…
Do you remember a tune in particular?

items.title: Sheila Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Middleburgh, New York, May 11, 2002
items.q: I’ve always given credit to the greats, which are Billie, which are Prez, which are Bird, which are Bud Powell, Monk, Ellington.

ctx.x: Yeah really. You know, if Bird was working at a club somewhere or at a concert somewhere, you know like a little dance, they used to have these cocktail sips, and he could ask me to get up and sing with him. You know. He must have thought I had something going on, that I had a love for the music, not even something going, but a love for the music. So I just, you know, that worries me. What worries me today, and I hope it’s resolved, is like this reverse kind of thing that happens once in a while with the younger…
The state of jazz these days seems to have found its ways of course into universities and the academic world. Is that a good thing?
